public_source_recovery.scope: Reproducibility transport progress only; artifact existence is confirmed, implementation semantics remain unverified.

design.purpose: Replace the prior parallel slow/fast proxy with one O(Nk)-class active tracker plus a bounded dormant-memory bank and local change/release statistic; test nonlinear observations, multiple persistent task changes, temporary latent silences, delayed/sparse error, tracker dependence, and a simple tracker-timescale detector normalization.
design.stream: Synthetic nonlinear latent stream; ambient N=24, latent d=6, active rank k=4, T=900. Observation x=A_t z + 0.18 B tanh(z) + Gaussian noise. Two persistent task/representation changes occur near t=285 and t=595 with seed-specific +/-25 jitter; one latent encoding rotates 35 degrees at the first switch and another 40 degrees at the second, plus an 8-degree slow drift. Two independent task-relevant latent modes undergo temporary disappearance/reappearance windows. Target readout changes across three tasks.
design.single_state_memory: One active N x k subspace plus at most m=2 dormant ambient decoder components. When an unsupervised tracker update rotates the active subspace, the component of the current ambient decoder that falls outside the new active span is compressed into the dormant bank. Dormant components can contribute directly to readout while frozen/slowly decaying. Sustained local prediction error clears the bank and temporarily increases tracker plasticity. This avoids a second full slow/fast tracker; subspace/dormant state is O(N(k+m)), excluding the bounded delay eligibility queue.

oja_like.description: bounded source-closer Oja-like orthonormal update; not source-exact SPLiT

design.detector: Standardized one-sided decayed CUSUM over already-observed prequential squared loss. A release clears dormant context and applies a 45-step plasticity burst; 120-step cooldown limits repeated releases.

calibration.selection: Combined calibration objective across both tracker families balancing total MSE, false releases, missed switches and release latency.

memory_churn.interpretation: The two-slot bank compressed many tiny decoder components produced by continuous tracker rotation. Memory admission was therefore not event-sparse and dormant memory alone produced no statistically resolved task-loss benefit.

interpretation: A single O(Nk)-class active tracker plus bounded dormant memory is implementable without the prior parallel slow/fast proxy, but this naive decoder-loss admission rule did not yield a statistically resolved benefit on held-out streams. Dormant memory alone was near-neutral and occasionally slightly harmful.

The raw common detector produced balanced but imperfect switch detection across PAST/GROUSE-like and Oja-like trackers under moderate feedback, with 56-66% switch detection and roughly 1.25-1.31 false releases per stream. Its held-out MSE differences versus plain tracking all had bootstrap intervals spanning zero.

Under 40-step delay and 25% label availability, release decisions became too noisy/late to show a resolved task-loss benefit. This is a direct negative boundary for this detector/memory design, not for dormant-memory mechanisms generally.

The tested tracker-timescale normalization did not make thresholds transferable. It increased PAST-like detection but sharply suppressed Oja-like detection, especially under severe feedback (71.9% versus 9.4% with the same common normalized setting). A simple CUSUM leak proportional to tracker eta is therefore not supported as a tracker-invariant normalization.

The dominant new bottleneck is memory admission/release calibration, not storage complexity: continuous micro-rotation causes high bank churn, and delayed/sparse error makes release evidence tracker-specific.
limits: Synthetic nonlinear latent stream; no source-exact recurrent SPLiT dynamics and no claim that these results reproduce or refute S8/S11/S12.
Dormant memory stores decoder components lost under subspace rotation; this is an engineering proxy, not an established biological mechanism.
Only one simple timescale normalization was tested: CUSUM integration rate scaled by tracker eta. Failure of this scheme does not rule out other normalization strategies.
Held-out intervals use 16 streams per condition; effects smaller than the reported bootstrap uncertainty remain unresolved.
The delayed-label update uses a bounded sample eligibility queue and is not a fully local synaptic implementation.

candidate_update.positive_scope: A single active subspace tracker plus bounded dormant decoder memory and local error release can represent the stability-plasticity mechanism without a parallel second tracker, at O(N(k+m)) subspace state. Raw common detector thresholds transferred more evenly across PAST-like and Oja-like variants than the tested eta-scaled normalization.
candidate_update.negative_boundary: Naive continuous decoder-loss admission causes high memory churn and no statistically resolved task-loss gain; under severe delayed/sparse error, release decisions remain too noisy/late. Eta-proportional CUSUM timescale normalization is specifically disfavored by the held-out tracker-transfer test.

exact_next_action: Use the now-identified Figshare item/file ids to retry read-only source recovery when transport permits. In parallel, replace continuous decoder-loss admission with an event-sparse, subspace-invariant utility gate: admit a dormant direction only when persistent lost decoder mass, covariance-energy drop and subsequent residual reappearance agree. Decouple change-statistic normalization from tracker learning rate; calibrate a shared standardized evidence rate or hazard model on disjoint streams, then test transfer across PAST/GROUSE-like and Oja-like trackers under the same nonlinear multi-switch/multi-silence environment. Add an unsupervised residual-change channel so delayed/sparse labels are not the sole release evidence. Report held-out bank churn, false-admission, false-release, release latency and task-loss Pareto. Keep all conclusions bounded until source-exact S8/S11/S12 code is recovered.
